title: Two internal/cli tests fail locally on unmodified main and pass in CI
description:
TestRunEpicFailsClosed and TestTheBuiltBinaryExitsTwo (internal/cli) fail on an unmodified origin/main checkout - both in the main checkout and in a fresh worktree - while the same commit passes both in CI.

A test that is red on the developer's machine and green in CI is no signal at all. It trains everyone to ignore a red local run, which is how a real failure gets waved through; and it means 'the suite passes' means different things in the two places that say it.

Per the standing rule, treat this as a bug rather than as environment noise. Both names suggest process-level assertions - a run that must fail closed, and a built binary's exit code - so the likely shape is a dependency on something the CI image has and this machine does not, or the reverse: a PATH entry, an installed binary, a git identity, a HOME-relative path, or something ticfac itself installed into ~/.local/bin during a session.

Determine which, and make the test either independent of it or explicit about requiring it - a skip with a reason naming what is missing is acceptable; a silent difference is not.

Reported by the agent implementing prs, which correctly declined to treat its own green CI as evidence that a locally red test was fine.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests give the same verdict locally and in CI on an unmodified checkout, or skip with a reason naming exactly what the environment lacks
